::: {#exr-giraffe-meet-cotton}
We have defined for your convenience several one-input functions named `f1()` through `f5()`. Graph each of them, one at a time, on the domain -5 to 5 and, from the graph, read off the requested information. (Hint: All you need is the *name* of the function, you don't have to worry about how we constructed it.)

```{webr}
#| echo: false
#| autorun: true
f1 <- mosaicCalc::doodle_fun( ~ z, seed = 504)
f2 <- mosaicCalc::doodle_fun( ~ z, seed = 506)
f3 <- mosaicCalc::doodle_fun( ~ z, seed = 508)
f4 <- mosaicCalc::doodle_fun( ~ z, seed = 510)
f5 <- mosaicCalc::doodle_fun( ~ z, seed = 512)
```

```{webr}
#| caption: Make your plots here.
slice_plot(f1(z) ~ z, domain(z = -5:5))
```

1. For `f1()`, for what input does the output reach its maximum value? (Select the closest value.)

```{devoirs_choices}
#| label: choices_gmc.1.lesle
- '-4':
    correct: false
- '-3':
    correct: false
- '-2':
    correct: true
- '0':
    correct: false
- '2':
    correct: false
- '3':
    correct: false
- '4':
    correct: false
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
Q <- devoirs_selection(
  label = "gmc-1-lesle",
  question = "Placeholder for now",
  answers = choices_gmc.1.lesle,
  multiple = FALSE
)
Q(inline = TRUE)
```
